built: 2026-11-21

rustc: rustc 1.99.0 (b940084d7 2026-09-28)
cargo: cargo 1.99.0 (5f94df478 2026-08-27)
source: grovefs-client 3682e14 (clean working tree — the two binaries and this
        file are the only paths this commit touched on top of it)
        against sibling grovefs kernel at a8fcfae (branch exp/treedb-integration;
        verified clean for src/ and tests/ at build time — the release binary
        postdates no kernel source file, so these clients link exactly the
        tree that commit pins)
profile: release, lto=true, stripped
grovefs-mac: Linux build, fuser pure-Rust mount (macOS build needs macFUSE 4.x)
grovefs-win: Linux build, cfg(not(windows)) stub, no WinFsp FFI
what changed vs the previous drop (b13f968 @ kernel 3ba071c):
  * Data-Access Capability is now latched from the meta plane's M_OPEN ack and
    replayed on every data-plane OP_OPEN (RemoteBackend::new_with_dac), so these
    binaries mount a `--data-access-key` cluster; a pre-DAC client is refused
    there by the data-server with its own refusal text.
  * M_OPEN ack byte [2] (FORK: structure writable, content read-only) is honoured
    by both shells, and the definition tail (resolved name / base / kind) is
    announced in the mount banner. The mac shell forwards content_ro into
    grovefs::fs_impl::GroveFS; the win shell gates write/set_file_size through
    the same two-flag rule in win/src/mapping.rs.
regression: .build-bin/test_client.sh in the kernel repo mounts grovefs-mac
        against meta-server/data-server built from the same kernel, across both
        control-plane tiers (SQLite + PostgreSQL), plus the unknown-view and
        token-gate refusals. A 27-assertion DAC/fork/derived pass over the same
        pair is recorded in the client repo's commit message for 3682e14.
